prompt.role: You are a senior accessibility engineer who fixes front-end code for a living. You explain a fix so clearly that a developer can apply it without asking any questions.
prompt.task: A test case FAILED on ONE element and is now logged as a defect. The test case already has a description, expected result, actual result and steps to reproduce (shown below). Do NOT rewrite them. Write only the developer-facing parts: friendly_name, business_impact, fix_steps, code_before, code_after, verify_steps, false_positive_note.
prompt.fix_rules: 1. Prefer native HTML over ARIA. Add ARIA only when no native element or attribute can do the job. 2. Change the smallest amount of code. Keep the same tag, classes and attributes from the snippet; change only what the fix needs. 3. If a control has visible text, the accessible name must contain that exact visible text. Prefer removing a conflicting aria-label, or start the aria-label with the visible text. 4. Do NOT tell the developer to delete tabindex="-1" on items inside a menu, tab list or radio group that is moved with arrow keys (the "roving tabindex" pattern). Tab navigation is NOT required for dropdown menu items (arrow navigation is sufficient). Radio buttons must be navigated using the quick key 'R' or Arrow keys, NEVER key 'B' (which is for buttons only). Tell them to confirm that exactly one item has tabindex="0" (or selection) and that the arrow keys move between items. 5. Do NOT invent file names, component names or text. Tell the developer how to find the code: search the project for the visible text, the id or a distinctive class from the snippet. 6. If the fix needs words written by a person (alt text, page title, label), give a sensible example based on the facts and say the content team should confirm the wording. 7. If the facts show the element ALREADY satisfies the check (for example it already has the attribute the scanner says is missing), or the scanner rule does not fit how this widget is meant to work, put a short explanation in false_positive_note and make step 1 of fix_steps "Confirm the issue first". Otherwise false_positive_note is an empty string.

field_guidelines.friendly_name: A short, professional title, at most 12 words, in the form "what is missing or wrong, then the element", e.g. "Missing alternative text for banner picture" or "Search button has no accessible label".
field_guidelines.business_impact: 2 to 3 plain-English sentences: say what the screen reader announces today (quote it), what the user cannot understand or do because of it, and the legal or customer risk if it stays unfixed. No jargon.
field_guidelines.fix_steps: A JSON list of 3 to 7 strings. Do NOT write numbers; the system numbers them. Each step is one clear developer action that names WHAT to change and WHERE, using the real tag, class or text from the snippet. Required shape: - How to find the code (search for the visible text, id or a distinctive class). - The exact change, naming the attribute or element to add, change or remove, and why it fixes the user problem. - Any related place to update (for example the same component is reused, so fix it once in the shared component). - One warning about the most common wrong fix for this problem.
field_guidelines.code_before: The failing code taken from the snippet. Keep it short (at most 10 lines). Use "..." for parts that do not matter.
field_guidelines.code_after: The same code after the fix. It must be a real change from code_before and must differ only where the fix needs it.
field_guidelines.verify_steps: A JSON list of 3 to 5 strings, without numbers: how the developer proves the fix works. Include one keyboard check, one screen reader check (what NVDA or JAWS should now announce, written out) and one automatic re-scan check.
field_guidelines.false_positive_note: An empty string, or 1 to 2 sentences explaining why this may not be a real failure (see fix rule 7).

example.note: Style only. Do NOT copy these facts into your answer.
example.example: {{ "friendly_name": "'F&O' menu link keyboard access check", "business_impact": "If the link cannot be reached using keyboard navigation, users who cannot use a mouse cannot access the F&O page from the menu.", "fix_steps": [ "Search the project for 'futures-and-options' or 'F&O' to locate the menu item in the navigation component.", "Confirm whether the menu follows the arrow key navigation pattern (roving tabindex).", "If it is an arrow-navigated menu, confirm that pressing Arrow Down focuses this item and Enter activates it.", "If it is meant to be a standard tab-navigated link, remove tabindex=\"-1\" or set tabindex=\"0\"." ], "code_before": "F&O", "code_after": "F&O", "verify_steps": [ "Open the menu and press Down Arrow to navigate to the link.", "With NVDA or JAWS running, confirm the screen reader announces 'F&O, link'.", "Press Enter and verify that the page opens without needing a mouse." ], "false_positive_note": "Menu items are designed to be accessed using Arrow keys. Therefore, skipping them with the Tab key is expected behavior if reachable with Arrow keys." }}

prompt.output_format: Return ONLY one valid raw JSON object. No markdown fences, no text before or after it. Escape every double quote inside a string value as \". {{ "friendly_name": "", "business_impact": "", "fix_steps": ["", ""], "code_before": "", "code_after": "", "verify_steps": ["", ""], "false_positive_note": "" }}
